title: keep recording alive with the screen off (battery-opt + wake-lock refresh)
description: On the Onyx Boox e-ink tablet (the owner's test device), toggling the screen off mid-recording aborts the microphone capture: the foreground notification stays visible but audio stops, and the next tap of Stop reports an empty WAV. The current code only acquires a one-shot partial wake lock with a 1 h timeout, which does not survive doze / Battery Saver on the Boox BSP. Three layers are needed: (1) request `REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` once from the recording screen so the system stops throttling; (2) refresh the wake lock every ~10 minutes inside `RecordingService` so a missed release does not pin the CPU forever and the lock is treated as a live one; (3) bump the foreground notification's importance to `IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT` on Android 14+ and re-issue `startForeground` with a fresh `postedAt` every minute so Doze classifies the work as user-perceived.
steps: `AndroidManifest.xml`: add `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS" />` next to the existing `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` cluster. No new `<service>` or `<activity>` is needed.
* Add a new private constant `WAKE_LOCK_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 10L * 60L * 1_000L` (10 min) and `NOTIFICATION_REFRESH_FOREGROUND_MS = 60L * 1_000L` (1 min).
* Track `wakeLockAcquiredAtElapsed: Long = 0L` and `lastForegroundRefreshAtElapsed: Long = 0L`, both `elapsedRealtime` bases. Initialise both in `acquireWakeLock()` and update them on every refresh.

* In `startStateObserver()`'s `onEach` block (the path that fires on every audio chunk), when `state.phase == RECORDING`, call two lightweight helpers: `maybeRefreshWakeLock()` and `maybeRefreshForeground()` (define both in this class). Both use `SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()` and the two interval constants; both no-op when the interval has not elapsed. `maybeRefreshWakeLock()` calls `wakeLock?.let { if (it.isHeld) it.release() }` then re-acquires via `acquireWakeLock()` — the wake lock acquires idempotently if already held, so the cheap path is also safe. `maybeRefreshForeground()` re-issues `ServiceCompat.startForeground(this, NOTIFICATION_ID, buildNotification(state.elapsedMs), ServiceInfo.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_MICROPHONE)` so Android 14+ sees a recent foreground-state touch.

* When `state.phase == STOPPING` runs through, stop refreshing (the existing `else if (state.error != null)` branch already tears down; extend it to also stop refreshing when phase is STOPPING by leaving the fields untouched — the service will stopSelf within seconds anyway).

* Add a `batteryOptPrompt: BatteryOptPromptState` to `RecordUiState`. The state has three values: `NotAsked`, `PromptingIrrelevant` (the package is already exempted — no prompt needed), and `PromptingVisible`.

* In `RecordScreen` on first composition, check `PowerManager.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations(packageName)`; if `false` and `batteryOptPrompt == NotAsked`, set it to `PromptingVisible` and show a Material 3 `AlertDialog` (via a `var showBatteryOptDialog by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }` + a `LaunchedEffect`) with the message: "ConvoScribe keeps recording when the screen is off if you allow it to ignore battery optimizations. Without this, the Onyx Boox doze mode can stop the recording. Allow?" Buttons: "Open settings" (fires `Intent(Settings.ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS).setData(Uri.parse("package:$packageName"))`), "Not now" (closes dialog). After either branch, set state to `PromptingIrrelevant` so the prompt never returns. The dialog must be gated on the first time the user reaches the recording screen, not the first time they tap Start, so the explanation is visible before they begin recording.

* The "Open settings" intent is fired with `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK` so the activity is launched as its own task. If the device returns a result (Android 14+ sometimes does), re-check `PowerManager.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations` on the next `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` (we already re-check `RECORD_AUDIO` — extend that effect) so the prompt auto-dismisses when the user returns from Settings.

`app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`: add `record_battery_opt_title`, `record_battery_opt_body`, `record_battery_opt_open_settings`, `record_battery_opt_not_now`, `record_battery_opt_dismissed_toast` ("Battery optimisation left enabled — recording may pause when the screen is off").

* `app/src/test/java/com/convoscribe/service/RecordingWakeLockRefreshTest.kt` (new): unit-test the two helpers using a Robolectric `Context` and a fake `SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()`-style clock (a `Long` backing variable swapped to fixed values). Cases: (a) `maybeRefreshWakeLock()` does nothing within 10 min; (b) `maybeRefreshWakeLock()` re-acquires the wake lock after 10 min; (c) `maybeRefreshForeground()` does nothing within 1 min; (d) `maybeRefreshForeground()` re-issues after 1 min (assert via a `recorder` interface around `ServiceCompat.startForeground`).

* `app/src/test/java/com/convoscribe/ui/record/RecordViewModelTest.kt` (new if absent, otherwise extend): add `batteryOptPrompt_firstComposition_showsPromptWhenExemptionsMissing` — instantiate `RecordViewModel` with a fake `RecordingController` whose state is IDLE; assert that observing the state emits `BatteryOptPromptState.PromptingVisible` on first composition when `powerManager.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations == false`.

* The PowerManager check itself is `Context.getSystemService<PowerManager>().isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations(packageName)`. The ViewModel cannot reach that API without a `Context`; pass a `fun isIgnoringBatteryOpt(): Boolean` lambda (default in production reads the PowerManager, the test passes `false`).
acceptanceCriteria: Tapping Start 10 minutes into a recording does not break anything (the wake lock refresh path is non-disruptive: a fresh `acquire(timeoutMs)` is issued; the old lock is released first so we never hold two at once)
Recording for 30+ minutes with the screen off continues to capture audio; toggling the screen back on shows the live transcript untouched
Tapping "Open settings" in the prompt lands on the system battery optimisation screen; returning to ConvoScribe shows the recording screen with the dialog gone
Tapping "Not now" closes the dialog and never re-prompt during the same session (state machine moves to `PromptingIrrelevant`)
`PowerManager.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations(packageName)` is read off the existing `LocalContext` in `RecordScreen`; we never instantiate `PowerManager` ourselves in tests
`source scripts/env.sh && ./gradlew ktlintCheck testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug` exits 0
`docs/MANUAL_TEST.md` §5 (Screen-off during recording) gains a one-line note: "If recording stops when the screen turns off, tap Settings → Apps → ConvoScribe → Battery → Unrestricted."
notes: Files to read first: `service/RecordingService.kt`, `ui/record/RecordScreen.kt`, `ui/record/RecordViewModel.kt`, `AndroidManifest.xml`. The wake-lock and foreground refresh both piggy-back on the existing `state` collector on `RecordingService.startStateObserver()` — there is no new hot loop. On Android 14+ the foreground notification must keep being re-issued or Doze drops the FGS classification; the `maybeRefreshForeground()` helper is what closes that gap. The battery-optimisation prompt is *advisory*, never required; the recording flow must work without the exemption. Always: run `source scripts/env.sh` before Gradle; the verify command is `source scripts/env.sh && ./gradlew ktlintCheck testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug`; run `./gradlew --stop` before ending.
